theme: National symbols deep — animal, bird, flower, tree, fruit, sport

questions.question: India's national heritage animal is the ___.
questions.funFact: The elephant was named India's National Heritage Animal in 2010 to help protect it.

questions.question: Hockey is the officially declared national game of India.
questions.funFact: Surprisingly, India has no officially declared national game, even though hockey and cricket are hugely loved.

questions.question: The national song of India, 'Vande Mataram', was written by whom?
questions.funFact: 'Vande Mataram' first appeared in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel 'Anandamath'.

questions.question: The national flower of India is the ___.
questions.funFact: The lotus is special because it grows in muddy ponds but its flower stays clean and beautiful.

questions.question: The national tree of India is the ___.
questions.funFact: The banyan tree grows roots that hang down from its branches and turn into new trunks.

questions.question: Match each type of national symbol to the correct one for India.
questions.funFact: India chose most of its national symbols in the years soon after becoming independent in 1947.

questions.question: The mango is the national fruit of India.
questions.funFact: The mango is called the 'king of fruits', and India grows more mangoes than any other country.

questions.question: Which of these does India NOT have an official one of?
questions.funFact: India has a national bird, flower and tree, but it has never chosen an official national colour.

questions.question: India's national aquatic animal is the ___.
questions.funFact: The Gangetic river dolphin lives in rivers, not the sea, and is almost completely blind.

questions.question: India's national currency is the ___.
questions.funFact: The symbol for the Indian rupee, ₹, was designed in 2010 and mixes the Hindi letter 'र' with the letter 'R'.

questions.question: The peacock is the national bird of India.
questions.funFact: A male peacock spreads its shiny tail feathers into a huge fan to dance in the rain.

questions.question: India's national calendar is based on which era?
questions.funFact: India's national Saka calendar was adopted in 1957 and its year is usually 78 years behind the common calendar.
